title: AI Safe Territory
text: Preface

title: AI Safe Territory
text:
What this book is
A place is more or less resilient to the erosion of human agency depending on its structure: how distributed its decision-making is, how redundant its communication channels are, how dense its civic life is, how exposed it is to capture by a single mediating layer. This book defines that idea, turns it into a transparent and reproducible evaluation index, and maps the result.
It is one project under the AI SAFE EARTH umbrella, and the source of the materials produced by AI SAFE EARTH’s Communicate pillar.

title: AI Safe Territory
text:
How it is organized

Foundations why agency erosion is the central risk, and why it is territorial.
The framework what AI Safe Territory is, and the pillars and indicators that operationalize it.
Methodology how the index is built, tested for robustness, and matured from sketch to instrument.
Application the pilot, the map, and the materials for community leaders.

Methodology chapters contain live code: the numbers in the book are produced by the same pipeline described in the text (see 9  Constructing the index).

title: 7  Pillars and indicators
text:
The framework groups indicators into two families — exposure & susceptibility (what raises risk) and agency-resilience (what protects it) — following the logic introduced in ?sec-resilience.

Risk is read as Exposure × Susceptibility ÷ Agency-Resilience.

Every indicator is defined once, in the machine-readable registry at analysis/registry/indicators.yml, which drives both the computation (Chapter 9) and the codebook (see the appendix). The table below is generated from that registry, so it can never disagree with the code.

title: 9  Constructing the index
text:
We build the composite following the OECD/JRC handbook (OECD and European Commission Joint Research Centre 2008): normalize each indicator, weight it, and aggregate. Every choice here is deliberate and logged; ?sec-robustness then tests how much the ranking depends on them.
The pipeline is registry-driven — it reads the same indicators.yml as the rest of the book, so the method described here is the method that runs.

import sys, pathlib
sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("analysis/pipeline")))
from build_index import load_registry, build
import pandas as pd, numpy as np

registry = load_registry()

# Demo data so the book renders before real data lands.
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
cols = [i["id"] for i in registry["indicators"]]
demo = pd.DataFrame(rng.random((6, len(cols))),
                    index=[f"territory_{i}" for i in range(1, 7)],
                    columns=cols)

result = build(demo, registry)
result[["score", "rank"]]
